entities.summary:
Democratic backsliding is a pervasive and insidious phenomenon where liberal democracies gradually become illiberal and authoritarian, eroding the very foundations of freedom and human rights. This complex and multifaceted process, which has been unfolding over several decades, has its roots in a combination of internal and external factors, including the rise of populist and nationalist movements, the increasing polarization of societies, and the growing influence of authoritarian regimes. As democratic backsliding gains momentum, it has significant consequences for the rule of law, the independence of institutions, and the protection of individual rights and freedoms. The erosion of democratic norms and values has far-reaching implications for the stability and security of societies, as well as for the global order.

The causes of democratic backsliding are varied and complex, but some key factors include the rise of social media and the manipulation of information, the increasing influence of money in politics, and the growing role of authoritarian regimes in shaping global governance. These factors have contributed to the decline of democratic norms and values, and have created an environment in which authoritarianism can flourish. The effects of democratic backsliding are equally far-reaching, including the erosion of the rule of law, the suppression of individual rights and freedoms, and the growing instability and insecurity of societies. The legacy of democratic backsliding will be felt for generations to come, and will have significant implications for the future of democracy and human rights.
